title: Sink deopt-only value promises into deopt branches
motivation: A value promise such as `n13 = prom-{ box(n) }` in `bench_ai_awf_towers` was made at version entry on every call. Only the deopt blocks used it, to rebuild the frame binding for the baseline. So each call allocated a promise that the normal path never touched. `queens`, `permute`, and `permute_fake` had the same pattern.
solution: `SchedulePure` gets a defer rule for a value promise: a one-block body that returns a constant, an outside register, or the result of one `box`. It defers such a promise only if each use is in a deopt branch, and copies it into each branch with a new body CFG and fresh register names. Only one deopt branch runs per activation, so the activation makes at most one promise. A new limit also stops any deferred statement from moving into a loop that does not contain it. `InternalInterpreter` accepts a promise statement in a deopt branch when it builds the checkpoint snapshot.

files.server/src/main/java/org/prlprg/fir/inte: The deopt-branch snapshot evaluation accepts a `Promise` statement and binds its register to an unforced SEXP promise.
files.server/src/main/java/org/prlprg/fir/opt/: Adds the deopt-only value-promise defer rule, copies a promise with its own body CFG, and defers nothing into a loop without the statement.
files.server/src/test/java/org/prlprg/fir/opt/: Adds tests for copying a promise into deopt branches, promises that stay, no deferral into a loop, and the deopt state.
